notes:
I wasn't able to research Isaiah 3, so I have no notes for you yet.

My first attempt tried to open eight sources at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin, Wesley, Calvin and Matthew Henry. That went over the tool's usage limit before any page loaded. When I tried a single page instead, the tool said I had no calls left for this turn. I never read any page about the chapter.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, because anything I wrote now would be unsourced.

**Next steps:** ask me again in a new message and I'll run the research in small batches so it stays under the limit:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, then Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, then Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes, Calvin on ccel.org, and anything relevant on the Reformed, Baptist, Lutheran and Pentecostal sites. Verses 4, 12 and 16–24 seem the most likely places for differences.
3. **Other views:** netbible.org notes and bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship, and newadvent.org and catholic.com for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'll also search for any debated popular teaching, for example on verse 10.

If you'd like, I can start with just one part, such as the traditional verse-by-verse notes, and add the rest after that.
